cards.text: Zechariah the prophet has been seeing visions, one after another (Zechariah 1:8-5:11). The angel who speaks with him has been showing him what they mean (Zechariah 1:9). Now he lifts up his eyes AGAIN, and something is coming out from between two mountains.

cards.question: What does Zechariah see coming out from between the two mountains?

cards.text: And these aren't regular mountains. I spent YEARS staring at dust in a junk drawer, and Zechariah gets mountains of BRONZE. Not jealous, friend, just saying.
Red horses, black horses, white horses and dappled horses, one color for each chariot. Meanwhile I've worn the same white apron every single day since I got here.

cards.question: Zechariah says only the white horses are strong.

cards.text: Four chariots, four colors, ZERO explanation. Zechariah's staring at them like I stared at the shiny new mixer the day the Millers brought it home.

cards.question: Zechariah is looking at four chariots he doesn't understand. What does he do?

answers.text: Asks the angel what they are

cards.text: Zechariah asks, "What are these, my lord?" The angel tells him they are the four spirits of heaven.

cards.question: The angel says the four spirits of heaven are going forth. Where are they going forth from?

answers.text: Their station before the Lord of all the earth
The gates of the temple in Jerusalem
A house built in the land of Shinar

cards.question: Then the angel tells Zechariah where the chariots are headed. The one with the black horses is going toward the land of the ___.

cards.text: The angel keeps going. The white horses go toward the west, and the dappled horses? SOUTH.

cards.question: The angel also tells Zechariah that the red horses are headed east.

cards.text: These strong horses are EAGER to go. Like me when the oven timer dings, and I've singed my mustache twice racing to get there first.

cards.question: The horses are eager to go, but the LORD tells them to wait at the mountains a little longer.

cards.text: Instead the LORD says, "Go and patrol the earth." And off they go. They patrol the earth.
Then the LORD summons Zechariah. He has news about the chariot with the black horses.

cards.question: The LORD's news is about the ones going to the land of the ___.
The LORD tells Zechariah that those going north have given rest to a spirit in the land of the north. Whose spirit is it?

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "And these aren't regular mountains." / "I spent YEARS staring at dust in a junk drawer, and Zechariah gets mountains of BRONZE." / "Not jealous, friend, just saying."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card cites Zechariah 6:4 but tells nothing from 6:4. Its only passage content is the four chariots and their colors, which is 6:1-3. Zechariah's question in 6:4 is the answer to card 7.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The mixer comparison doesn't match the action. Zechariah doesn't understand what he's seeing. In the backstory, Papa Dorin looked at new boxes sideways because he dreaded being replaced, not because he was puzzled. The line also calls back to the Millers and the new mixer. Bakers only know the junk drawer from onboarding, and nothing earlier in this lesson sets up the Millers or the mixer.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action. ... 6. A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: Card 11 gives west for the white horses and south for the dappled horses, after card 10 gave north for the black horses. A thoughtful baker would reason that east is the direction left over and mark True. Nothing on the earlier cards hints that the angel never mentions the red horses at all. The right answer (False) can only be reached by luck, and the card's setup points the baker away from it.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
